refinedPriorNodes.label: TaskExecutionClaimStore
refinedPriorNodes.refinement: R12 permits REMOTE_BINDING ownership transfer only through compare-and-swap after independent quiescence and replay-safety evidence.

refinedPriorNodes.label: ClaimAwareDeliveryCoordinator
refinedPriorNodes.refinement: R12 wraps delivery with a quiescence-attempt freeze gate so a source Binding cannot be re-delivered after failover preparation begins.

discoveredNodes.label: ExecutionQuiescenceRequestStore
discoveredNodes.reason: Quiescence intent must be durable before any external cancel/query effect so response loss cannot reopen the old Binding for delivery.

discoveredNodes.label: ExecutionQuiescenceProofStore
discoveredNodes.reason: Provider/task lifecycle evidence that the old execution owner can no longer execute is historical proof, not Task semantic completion.

discoveredNodes.label: ExecutionQuiescenceCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: Exact replay, remote correlation, terminal-state interpretation, pre-effect request persistence and provider quiescence adapters require one bounded lifecycle.

discoveredNodes.label: ReplaySafetyDecisionStore
discoveredNodes.reason: Whether re-executing work is effect-safe is distinct durable evidence from whether the prior executor stopped.

discoveredNodes.label: ReplaySafetyCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: Effect-domain replay safety must bind one Task/source/target/quiescence proof and cannot be inferred from protocol cancellation alone.

discoveredNodes.label: ExecutionClaimTransferStore
discoveredNodes.reason: Every remote execution-owner transfer needs exact replay identity, ordered history and references to both prerequisite decisions.

discoveredNodes.label: ExecutionClaimTransferCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: The actual ownership switch must be a local compare-and-swap after source and target preflight plus both positive proofs.

discoveredNodes.label: TransferAwareDeliveryCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: Any durable quiescence attempt freezes that Binding from subsequent delivery, including during provider response-loss ambiguity.

discoveredNodes.label: FailoverCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: Failover composes pure preflight -> quiescence proof -> replay-safety decision -> CAS transfer under three exact request identities.

flow: provider quiescence adapter or terminal-unsuccessful observation
authorityLaws: Cancel request or cancel acknowledgement is not quiescence proof.
Quiescence intent is persisted before any provider quiescence/cancel effect.
Once any quiescence attempt exists for a source Binding, that Binding is frozen from new delivery; provider response loss cannot reopen it.
A terminal observation may directly establish quiescence only when terminal=true and successful=false.
Terminal=true with successful=null is not sufficient; an ExecutionQuiescenceAdapter must explicitly prove quiescence.
Any historical terminal successful=true observation blocks failover even if a later provider observation regresses to failure/cancelled.
Quiescence proves that the old owner cannot continue; it does not prove that prior side effects are absent, rolled back, compensated, or idempotently replayable.
Replay safety is a separate target-bound decision. Recognized positive classifications are NO_EFFECTS, ROLLED_BACK, COMPENSATED and IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY.
PARTIAL_EFFECTS, UNKNOWN or any other unsafe decision blocks ownership transfer.
A source/target pair is structurally preflighted before any external quiescence effect; cross-Delegation or dirty targets fail without touching the provider.
The fallback target must be pristine: no DeliveryReceipt, remote observation history, quiescence-attempt history, prior transfer history, or existing Task verification.
ExecutionClaim transfer requires the exact positive quiescence proof and exact positive replay-safety decision for the same Task/source/target.
Transfer uses compare-and-swap against the current REMOTE_BINDING owner; stale ownership fails closed.
The Task remains RUNNING across failover and fallback delivery; only the R11 evidence/verifier path may produce semantic Task completion.
A late result from the old source cannot steal Task completion after ownership moved because R11 completion requires the current execution claim.
Transport/request idempotency is not promoted into a universal business-side-effect exactly-once claim.

standardsBasis.use: Cancel Task is an attempted cancellation whose success is not guaranteed; terminal task lifecycle and operation idempotency do not imply business-side-effect rollback or replay safety.
tasks/cancel is cooperative intent; acknowledgement does not guarantee work stopped, and a task may remain working or ultimately complete after cancellation acknowledgement.
